source.sha256_method: sha256 over 4 tables' full unfiltered COPY (ORDER BY <pk-or-natural-key>) WITH (FORMAT CSV) output, each preceded by a 'TABLE:<schema>.<table>' header line, concatenated in fixed alphabetical order: nq_basicdata.stock (ORDER BY code), nq_freefloatshare2.freefloatshare (ORDER BY code, date), nq_issueshare.issueshare (ORDER BY code, announcedate), nq_listcompheld.data (ORDER BY code, sh_chiname, sh_engname)
source.reuse_note: nq_basicdata.stock content overlaps byte-for-byte with the batch already pinned by security_master/security_profile/financial_facts/quote_snapshot/corporate_actions/sdi_disclosure/directorate, but this promotion's own correctness argument depends on the exact 4-table set it reads together (entity scope + the 3 ownership-specific tables themselves), so it mints its own self-contained batch rather than cross-referencing another promotion's pin -- same reasoning every prior promotion used for its own batch.

promotion.new_migration_reason: Like sdi_disclosure and directorate (the first two Netquity slices whose domain had no pre-existing value), no 'ownership'/'share_capital'/'holders' domain value existed anywhere in aiphabee_core.serving_dataset_domain_check. deploy/database/migrations/20260716130000_ownership_domain.sql extends the CHECK constraint (drop + re-add, the same mechanism the ipo_pipeline/hkex_news/sdi_disclosure/directorate domain migrations each used) with no table creation, access grant, or data load.
promotion.serving_dataset_domain_note: dataset and domain use the identical value 'ownership' (both are new values minted together by this promotion, so no pre-existing naming convention constrained a match, the same as sdi_disclosure/sdi_disclosure and directorate/directorate).
promotion.new_index_required_reason: entity_id lookup uses the leading prefix of the existing serving_record unique index (serving_snapshot_id, entity_type, entity_id, ...)

rights_basis.distinct_from_quote_snapshot: quote_snapshot deliberately uses its own 'netquity-market-data-staging.v1' policy version because market-data Web distribution rights were confirmed separately; ownership has no comparable separate rights determination and is covered by the original Netquity collaboration rights approval already used by security_master/security_profile/financial_facts/corporate_actions/sdi_disclosure/directorate, so this promotion reuses 'netquity-collaboration-staging.v1' rather than minting a new policy version.
rights_basis.account_context_independence: resolveOwnership filters aiphabee_governance.data_entitlement/aiphabee_core.serving_dataset by context.rights_policy_version (the account's platform.workspace_product_access.policy_version), the same as resolveProfile/resolveFinancialFacts/resolveCorporateActions/resolveSdiDisclosure/resolveDirectorate -- no hardcoded policy-version constant is introduced.
rights_basis.personal_data_basis: holder names (nq_listcompheld.data.sh_chiname/sh_engname/sh_simname) include individual substantial shareholders and directors (e.g. a chairman's personally-registered stake) alongside corporate/fund holders. This is the same statutorily mandated SFO Part XV / Companies Ordinance substantial-shareholder and director disclosure basis security_profile/sdi_disclosure/directorate already rely on for company/director/holder names -- a public-monitoring-data disclosure, not incidental personal data. No address, identity-document number, date-of-birth, or contact-detail column exists in any of the 3 promoted tables (verified below).
rights_basis.no_field_excluded_for_pii: verified: the full column sets of nq_issueshare.issueshare, nq_freefloatshare2.freefloatshare, and nq_listcompheld.data carry no address, identity-document number, date-of-birth, or contact-detail column. No field was excluded on personal-data grounds this cut; holder identity is limited to the same tri-lingual name shape already promoted for directors/SDI holders.

payload_shape_choice.chosen_shape: shareCapital / freeFloat / holders[] (each holder independently optionally carrying crossHolding)
payload_shape_choice.rationale: nq_listcompheld.data does not carry two independent row sets for 'general holders' and 'cross-holdings': every row is one substantial-shareholder-or-director holding record, and 'cross-holding' is simply the subset of those same rows where the holder is itself a listed company (shareholdertype='L') with a resolvable listcode. Verified: 644 of 9349 valid rows are L-type, all 644 carry a populated, correctly-formatted, resolvable listcode, and zero non-L rows carry a listcode. Emitting a second, separate crossHoldings[] array from the identical row set would duplicate the same underlying data in two places in one payload with no new information, which is exactly the kind of latent dual-accounting risk this cut's 'each bucket self-consistent' requirement warns against (verified twice via a scratch-postgres idempotency dry run instead of trusted by construction). Nesting crossHolding as an independently-optional sub-field of each holders[] entry keeps one array as the single source of truth (mirrors directorate's directors[] with independently-optional nested remuneration) while still exposing a dedicated, independently gateable field_path (ownership.holders.crossHolding) for the design baseline's separate 'cross-holdings structure' visual module -- the UI panel renders it by filtering holders[] client-side, not by reading a second array.

excluded_from_this_cut.sharecapitalchange_history: nq_sharecapital.sharecapitalchange (5,777 rows) is a share-capital CHANGE event stream (its own primary key is (code, effectivedate, sharetype), i.e. one row per historical change event, not one row per current instrument state). A per-instrument 'current share capital' cut has no single well-defined 'the' row to promote from an event stream without inventing a 'most recent event' derivation this cut does not need, since nq_issueshare.issueshare already carries a clean, genuinely current-state issued-capital snapshot. Deferred to a future slice per this cut's explicit scope-trimming allowance, not promoted or fabricated from a partial read.
excluded_from_this_cut.issueshare_sharehold_table: nq_issueshare.sharehold (13,140 rows, primary key (code, sh_engname)) is structurally a shareholder-registry snapshot, not a filing-event stream (no formtype/formno/reportdate columns), so it is not disqualified on sdi_disclosure-overlap grounds by shape alone. It also carries its own listcode field (integer) covering the same cross-holding edges as listcompheld -- verified: 644 rows have a populated, non-zero listcode, 643 of them shareholdertype='L' and all 643 resolve to a valid nq_basicdata.stock code, e.g. code 1038's L-type row (listcode=1, holdshareallper=75.674, transdate=2025-12-31) is the identical edge as listcompheld's code-1038 row (listcode='00001', holdshareallper=75.67, effectivedate=2025-12-31) -- so it is not excluded for lacking a cross-holding-identifying field. It is excluded instead because it is content-redundant with nq_listcompheld.data at the key level: verified every one of the 9,349 valid-universe listcompheld rows matches a sharehold row by (code, sh_engname) (the only 17 listcompheld rows with no sharehold match are exactly the same 17 rows already excluded above as orphan codes outside nq_basicdata.stock). And where the two disagree, it is on currency, not raw date range: both tables' sourcecode='SD' rows span the identical 2003-04-01 to 2026-07-07 window in this mirror (verified via sharehold.transdate and listcompheld.effectivedate), so a simple max-date comparison shows no gap -- but sharehold retains 3,791 SD-sourced (code, sh_engname) rows that no longer appear in listcompheld under any sourcecode, for companies that mostly (1,544 of 1,555 distinct codes) still have other listcompheld coverage, and these orphaned sharehold rows are overwhelmingly near-zero legacy stakes (mean holdshareallper 0.534%, median 0.022%) versus the mean 13.099%/median 5.161% of rows the two tables still agree on. sharehold has not purged shareholders whose disclosed stake decayed to negligible; listcompheld's list reflects the current substantial-holder set. Promoting both would risk presenting two disagreeing holder lists for the same instrument, one of them carrying stale near-zero holdings as if current. nq_listcompheld.data is promoted as the single authoritative holder-list source instead.
excluded_from_this_cut.freefloatshare2_partial: nq_freefloatshare2_partial.freefloatshare (18,239 rows spanning 2026-02-06 to 2026-07-06, but only 213 distinct codes) is a narrow-instrument, full-history free-float time series (verified: its own dataperiod row spans the full window, vs nq_freefloatshare2.freefloatshare's 2-day window), evidently serving a different (index-constituent historical charting) use case than a current per-instrument ownership snapshot. nq_freefloatshare2.freefloatshare (2,783 codes, most-recent-2-days window) is the correct source for 'current' free float and is promoted instead; the two tables agree on the 426 (code, date) pairs they share (1 negligible rounding mismatch out of 426), confirming they are not conflicting data, just different scope.
excluded_from_this_cut.sharecapitaldata_table: nq_sharecapitaldata.data (4,404 rows, only 629 distinct codes) returns zero rows for the validation chain (hkex_security_00001/00006/01038/02638) and its 'type' column values (ICA/OIC/ICP) have no decode/reference table anywhere in the mirrored schema (nq_codetable.* was checked). Coverage this narrow and undocumented, on a table that cannot even be spot-checked against this cut's own validation chain, is excluded rather than promoted on a guess.
excluded_from_this_cut.scsharehold_table: nq_scsharehold.data (10,060 rows, marketcode SZ/SH/HK) is Stock Connect (Northbound/Southbound) channel-holding data -- a cross-border trading-flow metric, not a company ownership/control-structure fact. Different domain entirely; out of scope for a share-capital/free-float/substantial-holder ownership-structure cut.
excluded_from_this_cut.nq_sharehold_shareholddata_table: nq_sharehold.shareholddata (a different schema than nq_issueshare.sharehold above, despite the similar name -- 8,387 rows, primary key (code, formno2, rectype)) carries formtype/formno2/reportdate/transdate/eventcode columns, the same filing-event shape as the already-shipped sdi_disclosure domain's source table nq_sdidata.sdi. This is exactly the SDI-overlap case this cut was asked to check for: excluded as redundant with the already-promoted sdi_disclosure domain, not promoted as a second disagreeing filing stream.
excluded_from_this_cut.listcompheld_orphan_codes: 17 of 9,366 nq_listcompheld.data rows (6 distinct codes: 935, 1178, 1367, 1369, 1492, 8088) reference a code not present in the current nq_basicdata.stock universe (verified; also verified absent from nq_ops.del_sec's delisted-securities log, so the exact reason -- code reassignment, privatization, or an untracked delisting -- cannot be independently confirmed from the mirrored schema). Their effectivedate values (2019-2022) are markedly older than the promoted rows' (predominantly 2025-12-31), consistent with stale entries for instruments no longer in the live listing universe security_master/security_resolution's own scope is built from. Excluded via an explicit WHERE code IN (SELECT code FROM nq_basicdata.stock) filter (the entity_id pattern must resolve to a valid current instrument), with the promotion SQL's preflight asserting this is exactly 17 rows / 6 codes so any future drift in this exclusion is caught, not silently absorbed.
excluded_from_this_cut.listcompheld_position_breakdown_fields: longposition_share/shortposition_share/lendingpool_share/derivative_share/securitiesinterest_share/duplicate_share (and their *_reported and holdshareoi_* variants, 20+ additional columns) are excluded this cut: they overlap conceptually with the already-shipped sdi_disclosure domain's positions[] long/short/pool breakdown, and promoting a second, differently-sourced long/short/pool-shaped breakdown from a different table risks presenting two disagreeing numbers for the same concept with no reconciliation contract between the two domains. holdshareall/holdshareallper (the single unambiguous total holding figure) is promoted instead. holdshareh/holdshareb (H-share/B-share sub-splits), holdsharevoteper (voting %, which can differ from economic % under weighted voting rights and has no cross-check available this cut), duplicate_sharetype (a rare classification with its own decode table in nq_codetable.duplicate_sharetypecode but only meaningful alongside the excluded duplicate_share figure), and totalshare/totalhshare/totalbshare (company-level totals that would duplicate, and could silently disagree with, shareCapital.issuedShares from a different source table) are excluded for the same self-consistency reason.
excluded_from_this_cut.issueshare_spac_type_field: nq_issueshare.issueshare.spac_type is excluded: verified constant ('N') across all 2,786 populated codes in the current mirrored snapshot (no SPAC-listed instrument is present), so it carries zero differentiating information this cut and is left for a future promotion if SPAC listings ever populate it.
excluded_from_this_cut.freefloatshare2_type_field: nq_freefloatshare2.freefloatshare.type (single-letter code: O/H/S/A/B/Z/U, no decode table) is excluded: it overlaps with shareCapital.hkShareClass (issueshare.shareclass_hk), which already carries the same share-class concept as a 2-letter vendor code; promoting a second, differently-coded share-class flag from a different table in a different bucket would add a field a caller must reconcile against shareCapital.hkShareClass with no documented mapping between the two vendor code sets.
excluded_from_this_cut.personal_data_columns: verified: the full column sets of nq_issueshare.issueshare, nq_freefloatshare2.freefloatshare, and nq_listcompheld.data carry no address, identity-document number, date-of-birth, or contact-detail column. No field was excluded on personal-data grounds this cut (see rights_basis.personal_data_basis).

entity_scope_choice.rationale: Like directorate, there is no comparable 'known but structurally out of scope' bucket for ownership -- any listed instrument could in principle have promoted share-capital, free-float, or holder data. Building the full 18,036-instrument universe with an explicit coverage.status=unavailable marker (quote_snapshot/corporate_actions/sdi_disclosure/directorate's idiom) keeps the distinction between 'no ownership data currently promoted' and true absence, and lets the new OwnershipPanel render a calm EmptyPanel state instead of an error card. Because this cut draws from 3 independent source tables with only partially overlapping coverage (2,786 / 2,783 / 2,753 codes respectively, union 2,807), coverage.status = 'available' whenever a code appears in at least one of the 3 tables -- each of shareCapital/freeFloat/holders is independently optional within an available record, the same discipline financial_facts applied per-metric and directorate applied per-field-group.

web.synthetic_counterpart: none -- like sdi_disclosure and directorate, ownership never had a synthetic scaffold anywhere in packages/workbench: it is a genuinely new tab, not a synthetic->live cutover of an existing one. The tab's status dot therefore has no StockWorkbenchSection key to read and renders neutral rather than a fabricated found/not-found state.
